Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 2-hour constant mid-sternal pressure (7/10) radiating to left shoulder/arm, onset with mild exertion (gardening).  
• Associated shortness of breath, light-headedness, persistent nausea.  
• Cardiovascular risk factors: untreated hypertension, untreated hypercholesterolemia, smoker, male age 54.  
• Recent exertional dyspnea, calf pain, and leg swelling suggest additional thrombo-embolic risk.  

Working diagnosis  
Acute coronary syndrome (ACS – unstable angina/NSTEMI) suspected. High likelihood given classic symptom profile and multiple risk factors.  

Supporting DDx (consistent with transcript)  
• Pulmonary embolism – medium likelihood; chest discomfort with dyspnea plus calf pain/leg swelling.  
• Aortic dissection – low–medium likelihood; abrupt chest pain in setting of hypertension though pain quality less typical.  

Management  
• Emergency transfer: ambulance activated and en route.  
• Hospital evaluation: anticipate ECG, serial cardiac enzymes, chest imaging, full blood work.  
• Advise patient to remain calm, avoid exertion, and withhold any medications until paramedic review.  
• Follow-up: clinician will review hospital findings once available; outpatient appointment to be scheduled post-discharge for cardiovascular risk management (lipids, BP, smoking cessation).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina/NSTEMI) – High likelihood: classic pressure-type chest pain with left-arm radiation, autonomic symptoms, and multiple CV risk factors.  
2. Pulmonary embolism – Medium likelihood: chest discomfort with dyspnea plus history of calf pain/leg swelling suggesting possible DVT.  
3. Aortic dissection – Low–Medium likelihood: abrupt chest discomfort in hypertensive patient, though pain quality/radiation less typical.
